field.label: Enabled
field.help: A disabled profile is left out of vpn.conf, so an OpenVPN server pointing at it refuses the connection rather than deferring it.

field.label: Profile name
field.help: The name the OpenVPN server passes to the script, e.g. auth-user-pass-verify "/usr/local/opnsense/scripts/OPNsense/SSO/auth-user-pass-verify.sh staff" via-file. A server that passes no name uses the first enabled profile. Letters, digits and underscores only.

field.label: Protocol
field.help: Which SSO flow the VPN client's browser is sent through.

field.label: Authentication server
field.help: Which SSO authentication server drives this VPN login. The list holds the OIDC and SAML servers configured under System - Access - Servers.

field.label: OpenVPN server instances
field.help: The enabled OpenVPN servers this profile protects. Apply automatically installs and guards the deferred web-auth directives on every selected instance. Leave empty only for legacy servers that are still wired manually.

field.label: Firewall host[:port]
field.help: Public host the VPN client's browser opens, e.g. vpn.example.com. It must resolve and be reachable from the client BEFORE the tunnel is up, and match the certificate the WebGUI presents.

field.label: Require the username to match
field.help: Refuse the tunnel when the username the OpenVPN client sent is not the account that just signed in through the IdP. OpenVPN keeps using the name the client asked for - it drives username-as-common-name, client-config-dir and per-user rules - and the browser login otherwise only decides whether the tunnel comes up, not whose it is. This is enabled by default and also refuses an empty username. Turn it off only when the server never uses the username for identity, policy, addressing or revocation and the clients send a deliberate throwaway value.

field.label: Web-auth timeout (s)
field.help: How long OpenVPN waits for the browser login to complete before giving up on the connection attempt (30-900).
